name: Loan term sheet
what: A lender's summary of proposed loan terms: amount, rate, amortization, term, fees, reserves, covenants and conditions.

fields.label: Lender
fields.definition: The lender making the proposal, and the mortgage broker or correspondent if one placed the loan.

fields.label: Borrower
fields.definition: The proposed borrower, often a single-purpose entity still to be formed, and the principals the sheet names behind it.

fields.label: Loan amount
fields.definition: The proposed loan amount. Where the sheet sets it by formula, record the dollar cap and the formula, such as the lesser of a stated amount and what the loan-to-value and coverage limits allow.

fields.label: Sizing limits
fields.definition: Each limit that can shrink the loan before closing: maximum loan-to-value or loan-to-cost, minimum debt service coverage and minimum debt yield, with the value, income and rate each one is measured on.

fields.label: Interest rate
fields.definition: The rate as written: a fixed rate, or the index, the spread over it and any floor. Note whether the rate is only quoted or is locked, and the date or event that sets it.

fields.label: Term
fields.definition: Months from closing to maturity. Record any extension options separately with their conditions and fees.

fields.label: Amortization
fields.definition: How principal is repaid: the amortization period in years, any interest-only months, or another structure such as stepped payments. When the term is shorter than the amortization, a balance remains due at maturity.

fields.label: Prepayment terms
fields.definition: The cost of paying the loan off early or releasing part of the collateral: any lockout, a declining percentage, yield maintenance, defeasance or swap breakage, and any open period before maturity.

fields.label: Recourse
fields.definition: Whether the loan is full recourse, partial recourse, or nonrecourse with carve-outs, and who must sign a guaranty and for what.

fields.label: Guarantor requirements
fields.definition: The net worth, liquidity and financial reporting the lender says it will require of each guarantor.

fields.label: Financial covenants
fields.definition: The tests the borrower must keep meeting after closing, such as minimum coverage or debt yield, how and how often each is measured, and what a miss sets off, such as cash management.

fields.label: Reserves and escrows
fields.definition: Each reserve the lender will hold, such as taxes, insurance, replacements, tenant improvements and leasing commissions or interest, with the upfront deposit and the monthly amount.

fields.label: Fees and costs
fields.definition: Each charge to the borrower: origination, application or good-faith deposit, exit and extension fees, third-party reports and lender's counsel, with whether each is refundable if the loan does not close.

fields.label: Conditions
fields.definition: What must happen before the lender commits or funds, such as an appraisal at a stated value, acceptable reports, estoppels and SNDAs, and credit committee approval.

fields.label: Binding
fields.definition: Whether the sheet says it is a binding commitment. Most say they are not; list separately any provisions that bind on signing, such as deposits, exclusivity or break-up fees.

fields.label: Proposal expires
fields.definition: The date the proposal lapses if it is not accepted, and any outside date for closing the loan.
